industry.title: Canada: Rising print/POSM costs and execution complexity
industry.text: Our outreach cited that “a lot of retail marketing teams across Canada are under pressure from **rising print and POSM costs**” and face more complex in-store execution — relevant given Kawartha Dairy’s owned stores and multi-retailer presence.

industry.title: US: High non-install rates for in-store materials
industry.text: Altavia benchmarks show **up to 70% of in-store materials are never installed** (with typical savings of 10–15% when optimized), underscoring the value of modular POS and better deployment — learnings applicable to cross-border retail environments.

talking_points: Could you outline your Retail Division’s scope across owned Kawartha Dairy Stores and how it interfaces with third-party retailers listed under “Other Places to Buy” in Ontario and Western Canada?
For stores like Ottawa, Barrie, Newmarket, and Bobcaygeon, how are freezer/fixture signage and window displays standardized today across differing footprints?
How do you plan and execute in-store materials for seasonal launches like **Reindeer Magic** and **The Tragically Chip** — lead times, approval flows, and end-of-season material disposition?
Do specific pack sizes (1.5 Litre, 11.4 Litre, 500 ml) require distinct merchandising or shipper solutions, and where are the pain points (e.g., endcaps vs. freezer doors)?
Are print/POSM suppliers centralized or handled by stores/regions; any consistency or cost issues you want to address this quarter?
For retailers in **Western Canada**, what co-branded display constraints or compliance guidelines most often impact your shopper marketing at shelf?
How do you currently verify in-store execution across your store network — audits, photo capture, or store staff checklists?
Would augmented or digital display elements be relevant at experience-driven locations like **Ice Cream Mountain** to boost engagement or upsell limited-time flavours?
Looking at holiday/winter items (e.g., Egg Nog, Candy Cane), are there upcoming activations where rapid-turn, modular POS could help reduce waste and speed deployment?
